title: TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer) entry
summary: A TLB entry caches a virtual-to-physical address translation. Format (x86-64): VPN (virtual page number, 36-48 bits), PFN (physical frame number, 40 bits), flags (valid, dirty, accessed, global, ASID/PCID, permissions). TLB is fully associative or set-associative. On miss: page table walk (4 levels, ~100 cycles). On hit: ~1 cycle.

structure.meaning: High bits of the virtual address (page number).
High bits of the physical address (frame number).
1 = global page (not flushed on CR3 reload). Requires CR4.PGE.
Process-Context ID. Tags TLB entries to avoid flushes on context switch.
4KB, 2MB, or 1GB. Encoded in the TLB entry or determined by page table level.

notes: TLB is the most critical structure for memory performance. A TLB miss costs ~100 cycles (page table walk).
L1 TLB: 32-64 entries, fully associative, 1-cycle hit. L2 TLB: 512-2048 entries, 4-8 way set-associative.
PCID (Process-Context ID) avoids TLB flushes on context switch (CR3 reload).
INVLPG invalidates a single TLB entry. MOV CR3 flushes all (or PCID-tagged entries).
Huge pages (2MB/1GB) reduce TLB pressure (fewer entries needed).
